title: Fill in the blank: memory and the stack
prompt: Fill in the missing mnemonics, registers, directives, and symbols that complete these AArch64 instructions.

blanks.prompt: Load a single byte from memory into w20, zero-extending the remaining bits.
blanks.explanation: ldrb loads one byte into the low 8 bits of w20 and zeroes every bit above it. Use it when the byte in memory is unsigned; ldrsb is the sign-extending counterpart.

blanks.prompt: Store exactly 2 bytes (a halfword) from w21 into memory.
blanks.explanation: strh writes the low 16 bits of w21 and touches no other memory. The h suffix selects the halfword width, which is 2 bytes.

blanks.prompt: Load a 64-bit value using pre-indexed addressing, updating x20 by 10.
blanks.explanation: The ! after the closing bracket selects the pre-indexed form. x20 becomes x20 + 10 first, and the load reads from that updated address.
blanks.hint: The exclamation mark marks the pre-indexed form.

blanks.prompt: Load a 32-bit value using post-indexed addressing, moving x28 forward by 8 bytes after the load.
blanks.explanation: In post-indexed addressing the offset sits outside the brackets, separated from them by a comma. The load uses the address already in x28, then x28 advances by 8.
blanks.hint: Look at where the offset appears in relation to the brackets.

blanks.prompt: Add a sign-extended 32-bit register offset (w21) to the base register (x29) during a load.
blanks.explanation: sxtw sign-extends the 32-bit value in w21 to 64 bits before it is added to the base in x29. A 32-bit register offset needs an extend operator, since the assembler cannot otherwise tell whether the index is signed or unsigned.

blanks.prompt: Define a macro a_s with a value of 16.
blanks.explanation: m4 expands define(a_s, 16) by substituting 16 for every later use of a_s. Naming stack offsets this way keeps the frame layout readable when the offsets change.

blanks.prompt: Create an assembler equate that renames register x29 to fp.
blanks.explanation: .req creates a register alias, so fp .req x29 lets the rest of the file write fp wherever x29 is meant. The alias is an assemble-time rename, not a separate register.

blanks.prompt: Ensure the following machine instruction is properly 4-byte aligned.
blanks.explanation: Machine instructions must start on a 4-byte boundary, and .balign 4 pads forward until the next multiple of 4. The operand of .balign counts bytes, not powers of two.

blanks.prompt: Calculate a stack allocation of -20 bytes while forcing 16-byte alignment.
blanks.explanation: ANDing with -16 clears the low four bits, so -20 becomes -32 and sp stays 16-byte aligned. The assembler folds the whole expression into one constant before the instruction is encoded.
blanks.hint: You need to AND the value with negative sixteen.

blanks.prompt: Set the frame pointer as a stable anchor at the beginning of a subroutine.
blanks.explanation: x29 is the frame pointer. Copying sp into it once the frame record is on the stack gives the body of the subroutine a base that stays put even if sp moves again.
blanks.hint: Which register is the frame pointer?
